hypothesis: The pinned loader repacks every Q8_0 matmul weight into KleidiAI's layout at load (dequantize, per-row requantize to int8, kai_run_rhs_pack_nxk_qsi8cxp_qsi8cx_neon): about 6 s of the ~8.4 s cold model_load_mmap. Doing that packing at build time and shipping the packed bytes in place of each tensor's Q8_0 bytes (they are smaller, so file size and offsets are unchanged) should cut cold model_load_mmap, the cold first request and the snapshot init by about 4.8 s (offline fixed-host: 8.06 -> 3.21 s), with no extra download time and bit-identical answers. Restore and warm should not change.

conclusion: Large, consistent cold-start improvement with no output change. Run 20261021T101749Z (us-east-2, 5 rounds, arm order alternating between rounds): 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, 600/600 answers per arm bit-identical to P1's reference. Matched by observed CPU part (/proc/cpuinfo 'CPU part'; no Graviton generation was observed or inferred), cold model_load_mmap fell 4.91 s on part 0xd40 (8.35 -> 3.44 s, -59%, n = 39 base / 45 e9, lower in 5/5 rounds; per-round ranges 0.08 / 0.09 s), 4.28 s on 0xd4f (7.20 -> 2.91 s, n = 4 / 3) and 8.09 s on 0xd0c (19.69 -> 11.60 s, n = 7 / 2). The cold first request (Init Duration + Duration) fell 4.87 s on 0xd40 (35.94 -> 31.07 s, -13.6%; every e9 per-round median 30.90-31.19 s below every base one 35.85-36.04 s), 4.46 s on 0xd4f and 8.22 s on 0xd0c; pooled -5.00 s, unmatched -4.90 s. Weight download is unchanged (25.01 vs 25.01 s p50 on 0xd40): the E9 file is 128 bytes larger, so there is no download cost to net off. The 40 SnapStart snapshot inits inside publish_version (each record's part from its own log stream, 0 missing, 0 ambiguous) show the same: model_load_mmap 8.11 -> 3.24 s on 0xd40 and 19.14 -> 11.24 s on 0xd0c, lower in 5/5 rounds on both. Load paths, from patch_e9.py's E9KAI lines: every 0xd40 and 0xd4f environment adopted the i8mm-layout payloads (nr=4, kr=8); every 0xd0c environment selected the dot-product kernel and took the convert path, which still skips the dequantize/requantize step and saves 8 s there. Restore (0xd40 -0.06 s, 0xd0c +0.15 s on 6/8 samples) and warm inference (-0.004 s 0xd40, -0.027 s 0xd0c) are unchanged within their per-round ranges, as expected: a restored environment already holds the packed model. Peak memory (Max Memory Used) is unchanged within ~20 MB in every class. Offline, on one 0xd40 DevSpace, the packed buffers the loader holds hash identical to the runtime repack on both kernel layouts (offline-verdict.json), and fixed-host model_load_mmap fell 8.06 -> 3.21 s. Cost of the run: $2.36. Host variability: 200 environments on three CPU parts, none reporting two; the cold effect has the same sign in every part and every round that drew it, is ~17x the larger arm's per-round range on 0xd40, and the unmatched comparison agrees with the matched one, so the CPU mix cannot explain it; no rerun is needed. Limitations: 0xd4f (cold only) and 0xd0c have few samples; within a round the cold and restore waves run one arm after the other, so drift within a round is not controlled (arm order alternated between rounds and e9 was lower in rounds of both orders); CPU implementer/variant/features, HWCAPs, core count, cgroup limits, kernel and AZ were not recorded and are unknown. Compatibility: an E9 file needs E9's loader, and a CPU without KleidiAI's Q8_0 kernels (no dotprod) cannot load it (the load aborts rather than misreading the bytes); none was observed. The ~3.4 s that remains is mostly the tied output head's runtime repack, which is E7's variable; E9 and E7 compound.

e9_vs_base.method: median(e9) - median(base) within each CPU part both arms drew (seconds; MB for report_max_memory_mb); rows with no CPU part enter no part; pooled_delta_p50 weights the per-part deltas by the smaller sample count

load_paths.method: environments by arm, CPU part and E9KAI lines in their 4 KB log tails (a tail can miss the init lines; those environments are not counted here); cloudwatch_lines counts every E9KAI line in the saved logs

host_variability.method: post-run, from this run's own records; no new invocations. Comparisons are within one observed CPU part; a part counts toward the verdict when both arms have >= 3 samples in it. Arm order alternates between rounds (conditions.rounds_meta[].order). Within a round the cold and restore waves run one arm after the other and warm passes alternate arm order pass by pass, so time-within-round drift remains a limitation for cold and restore.

metadata.cpu_part: observed: /proc/cpuinfo 'CPU part', read by the handler in every environment (row cpu_part)
metadata.ggml_cpu_variant: observed: the libggml-cpu variants mapped in /proc/self/maps after init (engine init log line). ggml picks the variant from the CPU features it detects; the record names the library only, not the features
metadata.threads: configured, not observed: 6 llama.cpp threads (row timing.threads)
metadata.runtime_version: observed: INIT_START Runtime Version ARN, pinned (conditions.runtime_version_arn)
metadata.execution_environment: observed: row lkai.env_id and the CloudWatch log stream name (logs/*.jsonl.gz)
metadata.snapshot_init_cpu_part: observed: the 'decider.engine init cpu_part=' line in the same CloudWatch log stream as each before_snapshot record (logs/*.jsonl.gz); unknown when that stream has none or two parts
metadata.snapshot_init_ggml_cpu_variant: observed: the same line's ggml_cpu= list
metadata.kleidiai_load_path: observed: the 'E9KAI adopt|convert|repack nr= kr=' stderr line of each environment's init (row log_tail / CloudWatch logs); on the base arm none (P1's loader prints nothing)
metadata.cpu_feature_flags: unknown (not recorded; /proc/cpuinfo Features was not read)
metadata.graviton_generation: unknown: this run recorded nothing that names a generation; never inferred from a part id or from timings

snapshot_init.method: before_snapshot records of the versions this run published, from the saved CloudWatch logs. A record's CPU part is the 'decider.engine init cpu_part=' line in its own log stream; a stream with no such line (missing) or with two different parts (ambiguous) leaves it unknown, and unknown records are counted here and in the pooled phases but enter no per-part comparison. One record per arm and part per round (rounds_meta), so per-round p50s are single values.
